status_summary: The work-requirement half is law and operative: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) raised the SNAP time-limit age for adults without dependents to 64, narrowed the child exemption to children under 14, removed exemptions for veterans, homeless people and former foster youth, and limited area waivers, effective on enactment, with USDA guidance in September and October 2025. The same law also requires Medicaid community engagement (80 hours a month) for expansion adults, implemented by a CMS interim final rule published 2026-06-03 (effective 2026-07-31; states must comply by 2027-01-01). The marriage-penalty half is not addressed in the sources read: a coalition letter to the House Speaker on 2026-01-06 treats welfare marriage-penalty reform as a future reconciliation goal, and a July 2026 report describes a bill to remove a marriage penalty in the state and local tax deduction cap, which is a proposal, not law. The interim final rule is challenged by 25 states and the District of Columbia in Massachusetts v. Oz (D. Mass.), where a preliminary injunction was denied without prejudice on 2026-07-29, so the rule remains in effect. A Rhode Island temporary restraining order of 2025-10-31 against early termination of SNAP time-limit waivers ended with a stipulated dismissal in March 2026 and did not reach the statutory requirements.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed; its SNAP section 10102 raises the able-bodied adult work requirement upper age to 64, limits the dependent exemption to children under 14, removes exemptions for veterans, homeless people and former foster youth, and limits area waivers, effective on enactment.
The same law adds section 71119, a Medicaid community engagement requirement for certain adults.
USDA issues guidance on the revised adult exemptions under the new law (ages 18 to 64, child exemption under 14, removal of veteran, homeless and former foster youth exemptions).

The U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (Rhode Island State Council of Churches v. Rollins, No. 1:25-cv-00569, Chief Judge McConnell) grants a temporary restraining order orally on 2025-10-31, written on 2025-11-01 (ECF 19); besides requiring SNAP benefit payments from contingency funds during the shutdown, paragraph 7 enjoins USDA from terminating able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWD) waivers early on the ground that they were approved for lack of sufficient jobs.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, D.R.I. (order, via CourtListener)

timeline.event: A coalition of conservative and faith-based groups writes to the House Speaker asking that a reconciliation package address welfare marriage penalties and phase-outs; the letter identifies no enacted change to marriage penalties in 2025 or 2026.
timeline.source: Coalition letter hosted by Rep. Grothman

timeline.event: The parties' joint stipulation of dismissal (ECF 53, filed 2026-03-02) ends Rhode Island State Council of Churches v. Rollins, and the case closes on 2026-03-03; the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse summary describes the dismissal as moot and notes that the waivers at issue expired 2026-03-01.

CMS publishes the Medicaid community engagement interim final rule (effective 2026-07-31): expansion adults ages 19 to 64 must show 80 hours a month of work, service, a work program, education or equivalent income, with listed exemptions, and states must comply by 2027-01-01.
Trade press reports a new bill that would double the state and local tax deduction cap for joint filers, described as eliminating a marriage penalty in that cap; it is a proposal and not law.

In Commonwealth of Massachusetts v. Oz (D. Mass. No. 1:26-cv-12962, Judge Stearns), brought on 2026-06-29 by 25 states and the District of Columbia against the CMS community engagement interim final rule's narrowed exemptions, the court denies a preliminary injunction without prejudice for lack of irreparable harm, noting the federal government's representation that it will fund 90 percent of state system costs, and states it intends to reach the merits by 2027-01-01; the rule remains in effect.

title: Eliminate marriage penalties in welfare and taxes; add work requirements for food stamps
uncertainties: The statute text of Public Law 119-21 was not read directly for this record; SNAP changes come from the USDA memo and the Medicaid section number from the c14-05 record and the CMS rule. Whether the law changed any marriage penalties inside the tax code (for example in deductions, credits or phase-outs) was not systematically examined: a limited search found only advocacy briefs, a coalition letter and one trade-press bill report, none of which show an enacted elimination, so the absence of change is an inference from limited evidence. The Foreword's phrase food stamps maps to SNAP. Related records c10-01 and c14-05 have more detail on each program. The SNAP time limit now reaches adults through age 64, per the USDA October 2025 guidance. The Rhode Island order of 2025-11-01 (ECF 19) was read on CourtListener and the docket history on the Clearinghouse; the Clearinghouse lists only temporary restraining orders, no preliminary injunction. Review of 2026-10-27: Ballotpedia News is a lead-only host and was removed as a source; its report that USDA guidance of 2026-02-26 kept the affected ABAWD waivers through their original end dates is an unverified lead, and the Clearinghouse page does not mention that guidance. The Clearinghouse summary gives the mootness ground as full reinstatement of SNAP benefits on 2025-11-12, while also noting waiver expiry on 2026-03-01; the stipulation itself was not read. The Massachusetts v. Oz denial was read on the Clearinghouse docket summary, not on the order (ECF 94), and sibling record c14-05 carries the same event; no later ruling there was found.
